format.name: agent-journal/events-jsonl
format.record_rule: a line whose top-level member 'declaration' is an object is a declaration record; every other line is an OCSF execution event carrying class_uid
format.upstream_validation: the pinned upstream OCSF validator is run on execution records only (every line without a top-level 'declaration' member); declaration records are validated by the reader against declaration_definitions
format.lifecycle: declarations are append-only and written before the first event that references them; a 'recording' declaration marks finalization (COMPLETED or INTERRUPTED); a file without one is an open prefix, or the writer failed, which only the ancillary run.json can state
format.ancillary: run.json beside this file is an index and summary (final hash, counts, failure detail, extension source, semantic contract, mapping audit); it is not needed to interpret this file and may be absent

extension.name: agentic_cli
extension.reader_rule: resolve class names through this table; refuse a file whose pinned uid/class table differs from the reader's compiled schema

time_policy.time: source-reported time when the record has one (time_basis 1); else the latest preceding reported time in the same artifact, else capture start (time_basis 2); metadata.original_time holds the source text verbatim; ordering is journal.sequence, never time
time_policy.severity_id: always 0 Unknown: Journal convention, not a vendor assertion

schema.definition_policy: each class, object and scalar type is declared before the first event that uses it: extension-defined classes and objects complete; core objects with their required attributes plus those the events use, amended by a later definition record when an event uses a further attribute; profile-only attributes of profiles the events do not enable omitted

cli.name: Antigravity CLI
cli.version_basis: declared from the live run, where it was discovered once per run by the documented adapter path `agy --version` before launch, because the stream-json output reports no version; the native session file was not consulted

launch_settings.command: replay of the sanitized live stream (original: agy --print <prompt> --output-format stream-json --dangerously-skip-permissions)
launch_settings.original_route: LIVE: CliCapture launch, raw stdout, independent byte copy

synthetic.label: SANITIZED REAL LIVE RECORDING (Antigravity CLI 1.4.6, always-proceed mode: an invoke_subagent tool step whose DONE record has step_type subagent and subagent_info naming the child conversation, streamed answer fragments over two agent-response steps, an undocumented system_message step; normal completion), replayed through the writer to produce this package; the live package itself is private steward evidence

written_by.name: journal-ocsf-writer OcsfRunWriter
written_by.mode: incremental: declarations and events appended as native records arrived; no batch conversion or re-layout

applies_to.launch: agy --print <prompt> --output-format stream-json (headless print mode), raw standard output
applies_to.selection: route stdout; the stream reports no version: the capture discovers it once per run with agy --version (RULE-8) and declares the basis

interface_sources.documented: Antigravity CLI headless mode documentation (antigravity.google/docs/cli/headless, fetched 2026-10-23): one init event, step_update events, one result event per turn; the step_update, tool_info, subagent_info, init and result members; status values; usage, num_turns and duration_seconds of the result are cumulative over the session, response is the turn's own
interface_sources.changelog: google-antigravity/antigravity-cli CHANGELOG.md at tag 1.4.6 (fd851f1da40e4347f1d05d211dcb45f94aede4c4): stream-json introduced in 1.1.8 with tool_info (canonical tool name, parameters, output) and subagent_info; denied_actions reported since 1.1.27
interface_sources.unavailable: the emitter's source, a published typed schema or SDK, and vendor tests; the CHANGELOG (1.1.8) calls step_type a stable, closed vocabulary, but its members are not published: the documentation lists observed values, and 1.4.6 emitted two more (subagent, system_message)

embedded.executor: journal-ocsf-writer AntigravityStreamMapper (direct Java); one record at a time; no cross-record state

time_policy.reported: none: the stream carries no timestamps (duration_seconds is a duration, not a time)

embedded.identity: agy.stream.step_identity.v1: a step's identity is its step_index, documented as the zero-based index of the step in its conversation (step_update.conversation_id, which every record reports), written as decimal text in tool_call_uid or item_uid with identity_basis_id 99 Other and the caption sibling identity_basis "Conversation step index" (the OCSF convention for an Other value); it is neither a model-facing call identifier (the stream reports none) nor an identifier the output stream assigns to its own items; in one stdin session the numbering continues across turns (documented), whether a resumed conversation (--continue or --conversation, a new process) continues it is not established. Scope: a step index identifies a step only within its source artifact (journal.run_uid, journal.invocation_index, source_ref.artifact) and conversation (session_uid); an equal index in another artifact, run or conversation is another step, and no continuity across resumed processes is asserted

tool_kind_table.meaning: a tool step is classified by the exact tool name the step reports (step_update.tool_name, documented as the canonical tool name); names absent from the table are 99 other
tool_kind_table.note: Name table only. The kind describes the request; no operating-system effect is asserted, and a shell command's text is never read to choose a kind.

rules.settings: working_directory = init.cwd, permission_mode = init.permission_mode (request-review by default, always-proceed under --dangerously-skip-permissions), model = init.model and agent = init.agent only when reported, tool_names = init.tools exactly; session_uid = the record's conversation_id

rules.content: none: the stream reports that a user-input step happened, never its text; the prompt a capture passed is caller-supplied provenance in the run's launch settings, not vendor content

rules.owner: item_uid = step_index (agy.stream.step_identity.v1, identity_basis_id 99); no response_uid: the provider's response identifier is not reported, and whether one step is one model invocation is not established
rules.content: one block when text_delta is present: block_type text_delta, block_kind 1 Text, text = text_delta exactly, text_update_id 1 Increment (agy.stream.text_delta.v1: an increment of the step's response text; the step's text is the concatenation of its fragments in record order, as the documentation's jq -j example joins them)

rules.owner: item_uid = step_index (identity_basis_id 99); the response the step belongs to is not identified
rules.content: the step's last text_delta fragment as one text_delta block when present, text_update_id 1 Increment like every fragment (it ends, never restates, the step's text); a step without text_delta has no content block (the stream does not project the response's tool requests or other content)
rules.usage: step_update.usage -> scope 99 Other with scope "Conversation step" (the unit is the step this event identifies by item_uid), status 2 Final (reported once, on the step's DONE record), aggregation 1 Scope total of that step (agy.stream.step_usage.v2: documented as the step's own token usage; one step is not established as one model invocation, so the usage is never stated at scope 2 Model response); distinct steps' totals are disjoint, the result's session usage covers them and is never added to them; tranches by agy.usage.tranches.v1

rules.request: tool_name = step_update.tool_name, arguments = tool_info.parameters exactly (absent when not reported), reported_state = state; kind by agy.tool_name_to_kind.v1; a step that became active, not the model's own request: no response owner, model call id or permission decision follows from it (in request-review mode a command step becomes ACTIVE and is then soft-denied)

rules.result: tool_result.data = tool_info.output when reported, else tool_info.error when reported, else no result content; with tool_info.error (documented: present when the tool fails) error_reported true and status_id 2, basis 1 Reported; without it status_id 0, basis 3 Not derivable (agy.stream.tool_outcome.v1: DONE is a lifecycle state, and a missing error does not establish success: a soft-denied command reports DONE with neither output nor error); a command's exit status appears only inside the rendered output text and is not parsed; the record's own tool_name and tool_info.parameters stay in its retained data (the call's name, kind and arguments are on its start, joined by tool_call_uid)

rules.owner: tool_call_uid = step_index (identity_basis_id 99): the same step whose ACTIVE record, as a tool step named invoke_subagent, started the call
rules.result: tool_result.data = tool_info.output or tool_info.error when reported, else step_update.subagent_info exactly (each spawned subagent's type_name, role, initial_prompt, conversation_id, log_uri, workspace_uris as reported); status as for tool steps (agy.stream.tool_outcome.v1); no child run is linked: the child conversation's records are not in this stream, and its log file is never read

rules.status: result.status: SUCCESS 1 Success, ERROR 2 Failure, any other documented value (CANCELED, INTERRUPTED, INVALID, WAITING, RUNNING) 99 with the reported word as its label; basis 1 Reported
rules.content: result.response, documented as the turn's own response text, as one block (block_type response, block_kind 1 Text, no text_update: it is the turn's whole text, not an update of a step item, and is never concatenated with the steps' assembled text) when it is a string, including the empty string the CLI reports when no text was produced
rules.usage: result.usage -> scope 5 Session, status 2 Final for this run, aggregation 2 Cumulative snapshot (agy.stream.session_usage.v1: documented as cumulative over the session of one process; a conversation resumed by a new process is not covered by the documentation or the recordings). It covers the step totals of the conversation and is never added to them; it can exceed their sum (on an interrupted run it reported usage that no emitted step reports), and the steps' sum is never substituted for it; tranches by agy.usage.tranches.v1
rules.permission: each denied_actions[] entry -> one permission decision 2 Denied at scope 4 Run, reported_decision denied (the member name), attribution 3 Unattributed with no candidates, method 2 (agy.stream.denied_action_attribution.v1: an entry names a permission action category (for example command) and a display name, never a step index; it is not linked to a tool step by name, position or text); the entry is kept as the decision's data

rules.selector: checkpoint, system_message and unknown step types, step states with no rule, unknown events
rules.session: session_uid = the record's own conversation_id when it reports one

rules.selector: any line that is blank, not UTF-8, not one JSON object under strict duplicate-key parsing, or cut off by the end of the source
rules.residual: raw_data (text) or raw_bytes_b64 (bytes); parse_status_id 5 Incomplete at source end when the source ended mid-record

rules.selector: a parsed record whose mapper threw
rules.residual: whole record in data; basis names the exception. A defect of the writer is visible, never a lost record

usage_tranches.meaning: cache_read_tokens, output_tokens, thinking_tokens (as reasoning_tokens) and total_tokens (as reported_total_tokens) are copied as reported; input_tokens cannot include cache reads (cache_read_tokens exceeds it on 9 of the 18 usage objects of the 1.4.6 recordings and in the documentation's own example), but the stream reports no cache writes, so it is the uncached input only conditionally: the uncached component is unavailable with measurement status 3 Conditional and conditional_value = input_tokens (agy.usage.uncached_input.v1), never the canonical tranche; whether thinking_tokens is part of output_tokens is not stated, so no reasoning relation is written; no member's measurement status is stated otherwise

unavailable_at_source: the user prompt's text (a user_input step carries none)
model-facing tool call identifiers and provider response identifiers
the content of agent responses other than text_delta fragments (tool requests appear only as tool steps)
a structured exit status of run_command (rendered into tool_info.output text)
the written content of write_file (its parameters report the path only)
the step a denied_actions entry refers to
a spawned subagent's own activity and usage (only the spawn's subagent_info is reported)

step_update/checkpoint.meaning: a documented step type whose purpose the documentation does not describe; it can report usage, which the result's session usage includes
step_update/checkpoint.disposition: retained-only (meaning not established); its usage is not claimed as a model response's

step_update/system_message.meaning: an undocumented step type observed in 1.4.6 between agent-response steps of a run that spawned a subagent, DONE with a duration and no other content

candidate.status: Antigravity contract 0.2.0-prototype (2026-10-23 close-out), candidate for the managing reviewer: tested candidate behaviour, not approved support. Changed from 0.1.0-prototype: a step's own usage is stated at scope 99 Other "Conversation step" instead of 2 Model response, and every text_delta block states text_update_id 1 Increment (extension 0.10.0-prototype). Retained meanings: a conversation step index as identity (identity basis 99 Other with the caption "Conversation step index"; no dedicated enum value), scoped to its artifact and conversation

facts: a tool step can end in state ERROR with tool_info.error {type, message} (read_file on a directory), although the documentation lists only ACTIVE and DONE
result.response joined the text_delta fragments of every agent-response step of the turn (two steps in the subagent run)

on the four completed runs result.usage equalled the sum of the parent conversation's agent-response step usage (a spawned subagent's usage is not reported in this stream); on the interrupted run it exceeded the reported steps (input 9422 against 6925): usage that no emitted step reports, whose origin the stream does not report
on SIGTERM the CLI wrote a whole result record with status ERROR and error interrupted (not the documented INTERRUPTED) and exited 1

in request-review mode a command step became ACTIVE, then DONE with neither output nor error; the result reported SUCCESS, an empty response and denied_actions [{action: command, display_name: RunCommand}], and the run ended without the remaining requested steps
a tool step's tool_name (read_file, write_file) need not appear in init.tools (view_file, write_to_file)
cache_read_tokens exceeded input_tokens on 9 of 18 usage objects, so input_tokens excludes cache reads; total_tokens equalled input_tokens + output_tokens on every record

mcp.target: a call_mcp_tool dispatcher step names the server in tool_info.parameters.ServerName and the tool in ToolName (basis 2 Reported dispatcher arguments, each only when a string); target_arguments_pointer is /Arguments when the parameters report Arguments; the dispatcher stays the call's tool_name and its parameters its arguments; one observed call stays one call
mcp.projections: the started step projects CallToolRequestParams {name: ToolName, arguments: Arguments}; a finished step reports its output as text, not MCP content, and no structuredContent or isError, so no result is projected
mcp.errors: tool_info.error on a finished call_mcp_tool step is tool_result.errors layer 3 CLI-reported tool failure with error.type as its code and error.message as its message
mcp.not_reported: the negotiated protocol revision, JSON-RPC ids, structuredContent, isError, capabilities and MCP content blocks
mcp.binding: ocsf/mcp/binding.json 0.1.0 (generated by McpBindingGenerator from schema/protocol/mcp/PINS.json); every projection is a partial projection typed by the 2025-11-25 binding because this route does not report the negotiated protocol revision; the projected members are defined identically in both pinned revisions

1.caption: Canonical single observation
1.description: The only observation of its entity and stage among the declared sources.

2.caption: Supporting observation
2.description: One source's observation of an entity whose consolidated canonical event is in the same file.

3.caption: Consolidated canonical
3.description: The canonical event of an entity and stage that several sources observed, built from their compatible fields with per-field evidence.

2.caption: Representation only
2.description: Equal values spelled differently (1 and 1.0).

3.caption: One richer
3.description: One observation carries members the others lack; nothing conflicts.

4.caption: Each richer
4.description: Each carries members the others lack; nothing conflicts.

5.caption: Conflicting
5.description: Two observations report different values for one field.

6.caption: Ambiguous
6.description: The identity repeats within one source, so no pairing is established.

7.caption: Single source
7.description: Only one observation reports the field.

8.caption: Superseded
8.description: A provisional observation of a quantity that a final observation of the same quantity (same scope, aggregation and model) supersedes: the canonical event carries the final one and the provisional one stays on its supporting observation, never counted again.

1.caption: Full reasoning
1.description: The model's reasoning text as produced.

2.caption: Summary
2.description: A summary of the model's reasoning, not its full text.

3.caption: Redacted
3.description: The source reports that reasoning occurred but withholds its text (for example encrypted or redacted reasoning).

1.caption: Increment
1.description: The text continues the item's text: the item's text is the concatenation, in journal.sequence order, of the texts of its Increment blocks. An increment is not by itself asserted to be the whole text, and the assembled text is never concatenated with a whole text reported elsewhere (for example a turn's own response).

2.caption: Snapshot
2.description: The text is the item's whole text as of this record: it replaces any earlier view of the item and is never concatenated with one.

1.caption: Monetary amount
1.description: Money in the stated currency.

2.caption: Premium requests
2.description: A count of premium requests the CLI reports as consumed.

3.caption: Model cost multiplier
3.description: A per-call model multiplier, or a sum of such multipliers, that a vendor reports for billing; not money and not a request count.

4.caption: Nano-AIU
4.description: Nano AI units a vendor reports.

1.caption: Scope total
1.description: The consumption of exactly the observation's scope unit (for example one model response); observations of distinct units of that scope are disjoint.

2.caption: Cumulative snapshot
2.description: A running total of the scope unit from its start up to the point of observation. It may include consumption before this capture began and is not the unit's completed total; two snapshots of one unit overlap and are never summed.

3.caption: Single response
3.description: The consumption of one model response within the observation's scope unit, which the source may leave unidentified (for example the usage of a child run's last response that the spawning call's result reports): neither the unit's total nor a running total of it. It is never summed with the unit's other observations, and it is the same quantity as another observation only when both name the same response.

7.caption: Child run
7.description: The run of a sub-agent that a tool call spawned. Where the unit is identified depends on the object (see usage_observation); its observations are never added to the parent's or the run's totals.

99.caption: Other
99.description: A unit the source itself defines, which none of the other scopes describes; the sibling scope names it (for example Conversation step). It is not established to be the unit of any other scope (a conversation step is not stated to be one model response), and units of different source artifacts are never joined by equal identifiers. Where the unit is identified depends on the object (see usage_observation).

1.caption: Reported
1.description: Copied exactly from the one native member named.

2.caption: Derived
2.description: Computed exactly from the native members named, by the declared rule in derivation, whose arithmetic the source establishes.

3.caption: Unavailable
3.description: The source reports related members, but they do not establish this component (derivation states why); the component is absent, never zero.

1.caption: Measured
1.description: The source establishes this exact value as a measurement of the quantity; for a running total, of every contribution to it.

2.caption: Possibly default
2.description: The source emits exactly these values also when it has no measurement (for example all-zero defaults); a measured value is not established.

3.caption: Conditional
3.description: On a usage component whose canonical value the source does not establish: a declared formula gives a result from the reported operands that is the component's quantity only under assumptions the component's derivation names (for example that a possibly default operand, or one that is only a lower bound, is a complete measurement). The result is the component's conditional_value, never the canonical value, which stays absent. A price estimate from it holds only under the same assumptions. Equal prices for the tranches between which the uncertain quantity could fall make that allocation immaterial to their subtotal; they do not make the subtotal exact when an operand is itself a lower bound, because no price recovers a contribution the source never reported.

4.caption: Lower bound
4.description: The quantity is at least this value, and that it equals the quantity is not established: the value sums measured contributions while a contribution the source did not receive, or for which it wrote its default, is missing (for example a running total that adds only the responses whose usage arrived and writes 0 for an omitted member). A positive running total therefore does not establish that every contribution was reported: a reported 100 is compatible with an actual 150. The value is kept as reported, never raised to a guessed quantity, and a price estimate computed from it is itself only a lower bound of the charge.

3.description: On a usage component whose canonical value the source does not establish: a declared formula gives a result from the reported operands that is the component's quantity only under assumptions the component's derivation names (for example that a possibly default operand, or one that is only a lower bound, is a complete measurement). The result is the component's conditional_value, never the canonical value, which stays absent. A price estimate from it holds only under the same assumptions. Equal prices for the tranches between which the uncertain quantity could fall make that allocation immaterial to their subtotal; they do not make the subtotal exact when an operand is itself a lower bound, because no price recovers a contribution the source never reported.

4.caption: Lower bound
4.description: The quantity is at least this value, and that it equals the quantity is not established: the value sums measured contributions while a contribution the source did not receive, or for which it wrote its default, is missing (for example a running total that adds only the responses whose usage arrived and writes 0 for an omitted member). A positive running total therefore does not establish that every contribution was reported: a reported 100 is compatible with an actual 150. The value is kept as reported, never raised to a guessed quantity, and a price estimate computed from it is itself only a lower bound of the charge.
